_meta.purpose: ECOCROP-style environmental min-opt-max per crop for deterministic suitability scoring (§C.9 ranking.engine).
_meta.source: FAO ECOCROP (Oryza sativa, EcoPortCode 1574) — data/raw/fao_ecocrop/rice.json (already retrieved, structured).
_meta.status: Merge-conflict correction (2026-07-25): the 'obidit' branch's aman_rice values were byte-identical to the pre-existing placeholder template, not actually derived from the retrieved fao_ecocrop/rice.json record it cited (TOPMN/TOPMX/TMIN/TMAX/ROPMN/ROPMX/RMIN/RMAX/PHOPMN/PHOPMX/PHMIN/PHMAX). Recomputed all three rice crops directly from that file's fields. His point that boro_rice/aus_rice should share aman_rice's range (ECOCROP is species-level, not season-level) is correct and kept — only the numbers were wrong.

aman_rice._source: FAO ECOCROP, Oryza sativa (EcoPortCode 1574) — data/raw/fao_ecocrop/rice.json: TMIN/TOPMN/TOPMX/TMAX, RMIN/ROPMN/ROPMX/RMAX, PHMIN/PHOPMN/PHOPMX/PHMAX

boro_rice._note: ECOCROP (data/raw/fao_ecocrop/rice.json) is a single species-level Oryza sativa record — it cannot distinguish Boro/Aus/Aman, so this is deliberately identical to aman_rice's range. Season differentiation happens via season_fit (crop_rules.json's `season` field), not here — a known FAO ECOCROP limitation, not an oversight.

aus_rice._note: Same species-level ECOCROP limitation as boro_rice above — identical range to aman_rice/boro_rice by construction, not an oversight.
